characterization_methods.key_findings: Alloy compositions were usually determined by ICP analysis; for the nominal 13 at.% Al polycrystal the real composition is 12.9 at.% (6.7 wt.-%) Al.

The coarse grain structure (of the order of 1 mm) of the polycrystalline as-cast alloys is revealed; as-cast alloys contain no second phases, whereas fine plate-like or rod-like carbides appear on grain boundaries only after slow furnace cooling from 1100 °C or prolonged heat treatment.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Specimens etched by an alcoholic 10% nitric acid solution

characterization_methods.key_findings: SEM was used for fracture-surface studies and qualitative precipitate analysis by EDX.
characterization_methods.purpose: Studying fracture surfaces and qualitative precipitate analysis
characterization_methods.technique: scanning electron microscopy (SEM) with energy-dispersive X-ray (EDX) analysis

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Philips CM20 instrument with 200 kV; thin foils prepared by electrolytic twin jet polishing at -30 °C and 12 V (7:3 methanol-nitric acid mixture), ion milling if necessary
characterization_methods.key_findings: TEM of deformed polycrystalline alloys revealed reduced dislocation mobility with increasing Al content, with cell formation observed only in the furnace-cooled Fe-12%Al alloy and straight dislocations/glide bands in the quenched condition.
characterization_methods.purpose: Studying the dislocation distribution after deformation

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Binary Fe-Al alloys with Al contents in the range 4-18 at.% were prepared by vacuum induction melting in Al2O3 crucibles using Fe with 99.99% purity (purified by zone melting to minimise the impurity content) and Al with 99.999% purity.
Solidification in Cu moulds to obtain rods usually with 18 mm diameter; the alloy was used in the as-cast state without any subsequent heat treatment.

processing_steps.method: electrostatic discharge machining, mechanical polishing and ultrasound cleansing in acetone
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Specimens were cut by electrostatic discharge machining, mechanically polished and cleansed by ultrasound in acetone prior to testing.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Yield stress determined as 0.2% proof stress in compression with total straining of at least 5%; specimen surfaces cleansed by grinding before testing.

Tensile tests performed on polycrystalline as-cast alloys of Table 1 (including Fe-13%Al); yield stress in tension equals that in compression at the same rate and temperature. At -100 °C the yield stress and ultimate tensile strength values are higher than at room temperature by about 80 MPa. No numeric per-composition strength/ductility values are reported for the 13 at.% Al alloy.
measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: cylindrical specimens prepared by turning according to German standard DIN 50125
measurement_conditions.strain_rate: 10^-4 s^-1 (tension rates between 10^-4 s^-1 and 10^-2 s^-1)

phases_present.phase_name: Fe-Al solid solution (bcc matrix; disordered/K-state short-range order)

structures.overall_structure: Coarse-grained polycrystalline as-cast Fe-13%Al (real 12.9 at.% Al) with a grain structure of the order of 1 mm and no second phases; according to the separate ordering study, noticeable short-range ordering occurs in Fe-Al alloys with Al contents in the 13-18 at.% range at temperatures below 600 °C during cooling after solidification.

unmapped_findings: Composition of the Fe-13%Al sample (Table 1, polycrystal row nominal 13): real Al content 12.9 at.% (6.7 wt.-%); impurities C 70-80 wt.ppm, Si 70 wt.ppm, As <30 wt.ppm.
The as-cast polycrystalline alloys (including Fe-13%Al) show a coarse grain structure with grain sizes of the order of 1 mm and contain no second phases.

Noticeable short-range ordering occurs in Fe-Al alloys with Al contents in the range 13-18 at.% (thus including Fe-13%Al) at temperatures below 600 °C during cooling after solidification; the highest degree of short-range order (by X-ray scattering intensity) was observed at 250 °C, and quenching from 1100 °C suppressed short-range ordering nearly completely.

Deformation twinning at -100 °C was observed occasionally for Al contents of 11-14 at.% (which includes Fe-13%Al) and in all specimens above 14 at.% Al; at room temperature deformation twinning occurred only for the Fe-18%Al alloy.
At -100 °C the yield stress and ultimate tensile strength of the polycrystalline as-cast alloys are higher than at room temperature by about 80 MPa.

The yield stress of the polycrystalline as-cast alloys increases linearly with Al content up to 18 at.% Al (described by Suzuki's theory of solid-solution hardening for bcc alloys), with a hardening coefficient of about 2.2 GPa; straight-line interpolation gives a yield-stress increase of 21 and 23 MPa per unit% for the 10^-2 s^-1 and 10^-4 s^-1 compression rates, respectively.

Ductility (elongation before necking and fracture strain) decreases with increasing Al content; ductile fracture with necking occurs up to about 15 at.% Al at room temperature and to about 12 at.% Al at -100 °C, with a transition to brittle fracture without necking in the range 15-18 at.% Al at room temperature and 12-14 at.% Al at -100 °C.

The fracture strain decreases steeply above 15 at.% Al at room temperature and above 12 at.% Al at -100 °C; both strain before necking and fracture strain show apparent relative maxima at about 8 and 12 at.% Al at room temperature.

Yield stress drops were produced only by Fe-4%Al and Fe-6%Al at -100 °C and are attributed to the interaction of mobile dislocations and (quenched-in excess) vacancies; no yield stress drop was reported for Fe-13%Al.

The linear hardening coefficient of about 2.2 GPa found here for polycrystalline alloys contrasts with the ~1 GPa reported for monocrystals; this is attributed to differences in alloy preparation (monocrystals annealed at 900 °C for 24 h and air cooled vs. as-cast polycrystals) and slip character (single slip in monocrystals vs. multiple slip in polycrystals).
